subject: chemistry
title: Molar gas volume
key_idea: (Higher tier, separate chemistry) One mole of any gas occupies 24 dm³ at room temperature and pressure. Use this to convert between moles and volume of a gas. Gas volumes in a reaction are in the same ratio as the moles in the balanced equation.

blocks.text: (Higher tier, separate chemistry) Equal amounts in moles of gases occupy the same volume under the same conditions. This section covers the value to use and how to convert.

items.meaning: The volume of one mole of any gas at RTP: 24 dm³ (24 000 cm³).

blocks.label: Volume of a gas
where: Volume in dm³ at room temperature and pressure.

items: It works for any gas: hydrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide or a mixture.
To find the volume from a mass, first find the moles using mass ÷ Mr.

diagram.alt: Practise calculating the volume of oxygen gas from its mass at room temperature and pressure.
diagram.question: Calculate the volume of **{m} g** of oxygen gas, O₂, at room temperature and pressure. One mole of any gas occupies 24 dm³. (Ar: O = 16)

items: One mole of any gas = 24 dm³ at RTP.
Convert between dm³ and cm³ by 1000.

blocks.text: (Higher tier, separate chemistry) The balanced equation gives the mole ratio. For gases, it also gives the ratio of volumes at the same temperature and pressure.

blocks.label: Propane burning
where: 1 volume of propane reacts with 5 volumes of oxygen.
3 volumes of carbon dioxide are made. Liquid water has a negligible volume.

items.text: 3.60 dm³ of CO₂ is made when propane burns in 7.25 dm³ of oxygen. O₂ : CO₂ = 5 : 3.

blocks.text: From a mass of one substance to a volume of a gas

items.text: CH₄ + 2H₂O → 4H₂ + CO₂. 0.40 g of CH₄ (Mr = 16): 0.40 ÷ 16 = 0.025 mol.
CH₄ : H₂ = 1 : 4, so 0.025 × 4 = 0.1 mol of H₂.

diagram.alt: Practise calculating the volume of hydrogen gas produced when zinc reacts with an acid.
working: Ratio Zn : H₂ = 1 : 1, so moles of H₂ are the same
diagram.question: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂. Calculate the volume of hydrogen, in cm³, made at room temperature and pressure from **{m} g** of zinc. One mole of any gas occupies 24 dm³. (Ar: Zn = 65)

items: Gas volumes are in the same ratio as the moles in the equation.
Use 24 000 to give cm³ or 24 to give dm³.

checks.q: State the volume of one mole of any gas at room temperature and pressure.
Calculate the volume of 2.1 g of C₃H₆ at room temperature and pressure, in cm³. (Ar: H = 1, C = 12)
2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. What volume of oxygen reacts exactly with 3.50 dm³ of hydrogen at the same temperature and pressure?
checks.a: The ratio H₂ : O₂ is 2 : 1, so 3.50 × ½ = 1.75 dm³.

worked_example.question:
C₃H₆ is a gas at room temperature and pressure.

The volume of one mole of any gas at room temperature and pressure is 24 dm³.

Relative atomic masses (Ar): H = 1, C = 12

Calculate the volume of 2.1 g of C₃H₆ at room temperature and pressure.

Give your answer in cm³.
worked_example.tip: The conversion to cm³ can be done at any point in the method.

worked_example.question:
Methane reacts with steam to form hydrogen and carbon dioxide.

The overall equation for the process is

CH₄(g) + 2H₂O(g) → 4H₂(g) + CO₂(g)

0.40 g of methane were fully reacted with steam to form carbon dioxide and hydrogen.

Calculate the maximum volume of hydrogen in dm³, measured at room temperature and pressure, that could be made in this reaction.

(relative formula mass: CH₄ = 16; 1 mol of any gas at room temperature and pressure occupies 24 dm³)
worked_example.tip: The correct answer, 2.4, scores all three marks without working.

worked_example.question:
Most cars have catalytic converters which catalyse the reaction between nitrogen monoxide and carbon monoxide to make nitrogen and carbon dioxide gases.

The equation shows the reaction that takes place in a catalytic converter.

2CO + 2NO → N₂ + 2CO₂

During a car journey, 187 g of carbon dioxide is made by the catalytic converter.

Calculate the volume of carbon monoxide, in dm³, removed from the exhaust gases.

Relative atomic mass (Ar): C = 12.0, O = 16.0
answer_points: Moles of CO = moles of CO₂ = 4.25 (1)
worked_example.tip: The mole ratio CO : CO₂ is 2 : 2, which is 1 : 1. The molar gas volume at room temperature and pressure is 24 dm³.
